63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment

74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])

All tests pass. The implementation in `food_chain.go` is fully algorithmic:

- **`animals`** — 1-based slice of the eight animals in order (fly → horse).
- **`comments`** — map of verse number → the second line (the "How absurd..." / "She's dead, of course!" style comment); the fly verse has none.
- **`catchSuffix`** — map adding "that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her" only to the spider when it appears as the caught animal.
- **`Verse(v)`** — first line, optional comment, then walks the chain downward (each animal catching the previous one) plus the refrain, joined with newlines. Verse 8 (horse) has no chain or refrain.
- **`Verses(start, end)`** / **`Song()`** — join verses with blank lines; `Song()` is `Verses(1, 8)`.

One bug was caught on the first run: the chain lines initially repeated the verse's animal; each line must name the animal one step up in the chain (`animals[k+1]` catches `animals[k]`). `go test ./...` and `go vet` are clean, and `food_chain_test.go` was not modified.
